title: Seasons and school years
goal: Find when a school year begins and ends.
prep: Write the four seasons in English.
Think: When does your school year begin?

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 03, entries 1–18
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Read & Listen: the main text
activities.instruction: Read the opening, Japan and the two US places. Listen again if you need help.

activities.title: Find the calendar details
activities.instruction: Find the start, the end and the summer holiday length for Japan and the two US places.

activities.title: Workbook · page 1
activities.instruction: Answer the two questions. Explain why Japan is different.

timing: Read Japan and the US examples
check: Ask for a season, an end point and a holiday length. Check the fact before correcting the sentence.
support: Model one comparison. Then let pairs find a second one without your model.
exit: Say why Japan’s summer holiday does not end its school year.

title: Different holidays, different calendars
goal: Compare holidays and the length of a school year.
prep: Write one question about a school holiday.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 03, entries 19–36
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: England, the UAE and Jersey
activities.instruction: Read the remaining places. Find a season and a holiday length in each one.

activities.title: Read & Listen: compare the places
activities.instruction: Listen to the remaining sections. Read the final section about the length of a school year.

activities.title: Workbook · page 3, Part C
activities.instruction: Answer the calendar questions. Use the text as evidence.

timing: Compare dates, seasons and holiday lengths
check: Distinguish a whole school-year span from uninterrupted lessons. Accept about nine months in Anchorage and about eleven in Kent.
support: Use a three-part prompt: starts / ends / summer holiday. Remove it for the final comparison.
exit: Explain one difference between Anchorage and Miami-Dade.

title: WhatsApp from Argentina: routines
goal: Describe a routine with I and he.
prep: Think about how you get to school.
Prepare one sentence beginning with I.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 03, entries 37–55
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: A Horse Before Class · WhatsApp
activities.instruction: Read Carlito’s message. Find who travels with him and how far they travel.

activities.title: Present Simple A · slides 1–27
activities.instruction: Work on routines and third-person forms. Stop after the first writing task.

activities.title: Workbook · page 2
activities.instruction: Answer the reading questions and write two facts about Carlito.

timing: Routines and third person: selected slides
check: Look for he rides and he wants. The factual content and the third-person ending are separate checks.
support: Contrast I ride with he rides. Ask for a new sentence before showing the answer slide.
exit: Answer Carlito’s question in one or two sentences.

title: What we do and do not do
goal: Write clear negative sentences about routines.
prep: Bring the two sentences you wrote about Carlito.
Think of one thing you do not do on school mornings.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 04, entries 1–18
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Present Simple A · slides 28–46
activities.instruction: Practise do not and does not. Use the base verb after does not.

activities.title: Words in Context · set 4
activities.instruction: Choose the meaning that fits. Write your own sentence at the writing stop.

activities.title: Writing sheet · Part A
activities.instruction: In your notebook, write your routine, a friend’s routine and one negative sentence.

check: A correct negative needs both the meaning and the base verb. Do not accept doesn’t walks.
support: Keep the original meaning when correcting a sentence. Check be separately from action verbs.
exit: Write one true sentence with does not about a friend.

title: Email from India: questions and teamwork
goal: Ask and answer questions about a journey.
prep: Write one question beginning with Do or Does.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 04, entries 19–36
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Four Kilometres Together · email
activities.instruction: Read Samuel’s email. Find how his brothers help him.

activities.title: Present Simple B · slides 1–17
activities.instruction: Practise do/does questions and short answers.

activities.title: Workbook · page 4
activities.instruction: Answer the reading questions and practise the question forms.

check: Require a detail from Samuel’s route. Ask who helps, how they help and how far they travel.
support: Use a short answer first, then a full sentence. Keep the routine tied to the documentary period.
exit: Ask a clear question about Samuel’s journey and answer it.

title: Ask a partner about the journey
goal: Use question words and frequency words in a conversation.
prep: Prepare two questions about a journey to school.
Think of something you usually do and something you sometimes do.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 04, entries 37–55
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Present Simple B · slides 18–43
activities.instruction: Practise question words, frequency words and the pair conversation.

activities.title: Writing sheet · Part B
activities.instruction: Ask a partner how they travel and what they do after school. Record the answers.

activities.title: Workbook · page 4, Your turn
activities.instruction: Answer Samuel’s question. Compare your journey with his.

check: Who, where, when and how must match the information requested. A subject question such as Who helps Samuel? does not take does.
support: Let students rehearse with prompts, then ask a new partner without the prompts.
exit: Write one question and one sentence about your partner.

title: Instagram from the islands: listen first
goal: Find the main idea and details in a recording.
prep: Bring headphones if you will listen on your own.
Think about travelling across water. Keep the boat text closed until you listen.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 05, entries 1–18
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Listen First · the school boat
activities.instruction: Listen once for the main idea, then for details. Answer before opening the transcript.

activities.title: The School Boat · Instagram
activities.instruction: After listening, read Zoe and Isaac’s post and check your answers.

activities.title: Workbook · page 5
activities.instruction: Take notes and compare the boat journey with an earlier message.

check: Look for another island, five minutes and walking after the boat trip. Sometimes does not mean always.
support: Replay the relevant part at the selected speed. Open the transcript only after an independent attempt.
exit: Give one similarity and one difference between two documented journeys.

title: Write a reply
goal: Write a relevant reply of 50–70 words.
prep: Choose Carlito, Samuel, or Zoe and Isaac as your reader.
Plan an answer to the question at the end of that message.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 05, entries 19–36
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Choose a message to answer
activities.instruction: Choose the WhatsApp message, email or Instagram post. Find the sender’s question.

activities.title: Words in Context · set 9
activities.instruction: Review meanings. Choose two suitable vocabulary entries for your reply.

activities.title: Workbook · page 6
activities.instruction: Plan and write your reply. Include a negative, a frequency word and two vocabulary entries.

check: Assess whether the reply answers the sender’s question before checking grammar. Check meaning, detail, cohesion and independent use.
support: Offer a planning prompt when needed. Avoid giving a full model before the student writes.
exit: Improve two sentences after feedback and explain one change.

title: Review and use it independently
goal: Use the unit language without a visible model.
prep: Choose three vocabulary entries you want to use without help.

activities.title: Vocabulary · Group 05, entries 37–55
activities.instruction: Preview this batch. Choose three to five entries for active use; stop at the end of the stated range.

activities.title: Words in Context · set 11
activities.instruction: Review the final set. Explain your choices and write an original sentence.

activities.title: Compare two messages from memory
activities.instruction: Keep the texts closed while you write one similarity and one difference. Open them to check afterwards.

activities.title: Workbook · page 6, new reply
activities.instruction: Choose a different reader and write a new reply in your notebook without copying your first draft.

timing: New reply to a different reader
check: Use the new reply and comparison as evidence. Completing a checklist or viewing 165 entries does not establish mastery.
support: Record the specific difficulty. Use the reserve meeting for a short targeted task, then reassess.
exit: Identify one skill you can now use and one you still need to practise.
